reason: Verified in source and by driving the page. render-b.js:515 handles data-act="add" as `var first = root.querySelector('.b-item'); if (first) openEditor(root, first);` — it opens the FIRST existing moment's editor. Driven at 1440x960 on owner-flight: .b-item count is 7 before and 7 after; #b-edit-title comes up pre-filled 'Menu tasting at The Orchard' with 'Delete this moment' beneath it; document.activeElement is still BUTTON[data-act=add], so a keyboard user gets no signal at all. A button labelled 'Add a moment' that silently opens a destructive editor on someone else's existing item is worse than a dead control, and this direction already owns the honest alternative — inert() exists at render-b.js:257 and is used at :613 for 'Nothing to preview yet'. Second half also holds: the editor's title input (render-b.js:416) is a value-only field with no input/change/blur handler anywhere in the file; typing 'Send the invitations to everyone' and pressing Done leaves the row, its data-full and its .b-grab aria-label all reading the original title. On the surface whose whole subject is one person's own words, the only field that holds those words discards them without a word. Neither claim restates the gates: interaction-check.mjs touches #b-edit-title only to prove native Ctrl+Z is not hijacked (line 462) and never asserts title persistence or add behaviour; audit.mjs is palette/type/contrast/geometry. Not taste, not a constraint breach, not already handled. One factual nit that does not change the verdict: the finding predicts the row would read the clamped 'Send the invitations' — in fact nothing is written at all, so the defect is slightly worse than described, not milder.
sharpenedFix: The fix aims at the right file but at the wrong writer. Every derived string on a row (grabLabel at render-b.js:81, re-applied by setAway:331 and setVisibility:358) reads record.title from recordFor() over F.milestones — so writing only data-full on the .b-title node leaves the old name in the accessible name and lets the NEXT step press resurrect it. Rename must go through the record: on the title input's 'input' event set record.title = value, then set the row's .b-title data-full to the same string and call C.settle() (C is window.__TLCORE, whose settle re-runs the word-safe clamp over [data-clamp] and then calls the direction's own settle to re-place rows) and refresh the .b-grab aria-label via grabLabel(record, item.getAttribute('data-date'), Number(item.getAttribute('data-away')), item.getAttribute('data-visibility') === 'hidden'). Do NOT push a {kind:'title'} entry into the existing `history` array as written: undo() (render-b.js:483) unconditionally calls setAway(root, item, last.from) and paintUndo() unconditionally computes Math.abs(top.to - top.from), so a title entry would move the row to NaN and print 'moved NaN days'. Either give both functions an explicit kind switch (restore record.title on undo; sentence 'Last change: renamed to X.') or keep rename out of the undo bar for now — the untracked-rename version is still an improvement over discarding the text. For add, prefer the one-line honest change now: replace act('Add a moment', …) in ownerSurface (render-b.js:559) with inert('Adding a moment is not built yet'), which is the direction's own stated rule and removes a control that currently opens a delete affordance on an unrelated moment. Add two assertions to interaction-check.mjs: a typed title survives Done in the row text, data-full and the .b-grab aria-label; and the add affordance either increases .b-item count or is not a button element.
